div.head: Ger 9
div.ab: [9] Me mæig in Maio ⁊ Iunio ⁊ Iulio on sumera fealgian, myxendincgan ut dragan, lochyrdla tilian, sceap scyran, bytlian, boteatan, tynan, tymbrian, wudian, weodian, faldian, fiscwer ⁊ mylne macian;

Me mæig inmaio 7 iun. 7 iulio onsume|ra fealgian . myxendincgan ut dra|gan. Lochyrdla tilian . sceap scyran . byt|lian . boteatan . tynan . tymbrian . wu|dian . weodian . faldian . fiscwer . 7 myl|ne macian.
He mæig in Maio and Iunio and Iulio on sumera fealgian, myxendincgan ut dragan, lochyrdla tilian, sceap scyran, bytlian, boteatan, tynan, tymbrian, wudian, weodian, faldian, fiscwer and mylne macian.

Man kann im Mai und Juni und Juli im Sommer [Acker] felgen, Mistdung herausziehen, Hürden herstellen, Schafe scheeren, bauen, ausbessern, zäunen, bauen, Holz schneiden, Unkraut jäten, Hürden bauen, Fischwehr und [Wasser-]Mühle machen;

In May and June and July, in summer, one can harrow [fallow land], carry out dung, make hurdles, shear sheep, build, repair, fence, build [in timber], cut wood, weed, make folds, make a fish-weir and a [water-]mill;

One should in May and June and July during the summer [set land] to fallow, take out dung [from] the manure pile, build hurdles for the sheep folds, shear sheep, build, repair, set hedges, build, cut wood, weed, construct sheepfolds and make fish weirs and mills.

In May, June, and July over the summer, one must plow the fields, spread the manure from the dung pile, prepare fences for the sheepfolds, shear the sheep, build, repair, enclose, construct, chop wood, weed, erect the sheepfolds, and make fish weirs and mills.
div.note: K: ‘Iunio 7’ supplied from Liebermann (June had dropped out); ‘bytlian.’ corrected to ‘bytlian,’. ‘Me’ for ‘man’ is attested in the 12th century (Mätzner). ‘myxendincgan’ has -n declension, as Rect 14. ‘boteatan’: compare Napier, Pogatscher. Liebermann compares Rect 2, 4.1a, and Gerefa 16.

Bilder Agsächs. Kalender stellen die landwirtschaftliche Arbeit jedes Monats dar; vgl. Turner Anglo-Saxons App. IV; Leo Rectitudines 207. Über die Egge u. 17. Worte aus Cato De re rust. waren vielleicht in des Verfs. Erinnerung: quae opera per imbrem: villam purgari; stercus foras efferri; bubile, ovile, villam purgato

Pictures in Anglo-Saxon calendars depict the agricultural work of each month; cf. Turner Anglo-Saxons App. IV; Leo Rectitudines 207. On the harrow below 17. Words from Cato De re rust. were perhaps in the author’s memory: quae opera per imbrem: villam purgari; stercus foras efferri; bubile, ovile, villam purgato

Toller Suppl. übersetzt botetan: ‘to repair’.—Vgl. Gl Zaun 3. Die Bauern zu Stoke besorgen für 1 Hufe: 16 gyrda gafoltininga (Zaunarbeit als Grundfron für die Domäne) in ihrer Freizeit; Birch 594.—Sk-Wi tymbrian . . weodian: ‘mit Bauholz bauen, . . roden’ [dies falsch].—Zur Fischwehr vgl. Gl Fisch 4—b

Toller Suppl. translates botetan: ‘to repair’.—Cf. Gl Zaun 3. The peasants at Stoke provide for each hide 16 gyrda gafoltininga (fence-work as a labour service owed from the land to the demesne) in their free time; Birch 594.—Sk-Wi tymbrian . . weodian: ‘to build with timber, . . to clear’ [this is wrong].—On the fish-weir cf. Gl Fisch 4—b
